Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the note. I pulled together a concise MAP-focused playbook and the workbook you can drop into internal review. Key points below (attached: MAP-Cost-Workbook.xlsx, eval-prompt-suite-v1.jsonl, redwood-map-checklist.pdf):

1) tokens / $ (approx, billed hosted API)
- "Small" chat (quantized 8-bit variant): ~0.6 tokens per millisec-agg -> equivalent to $0.0008 per token for typical dialog mixes; baseline: 25 tokens per user turn average
- "Large" chat (full-precision opt): ~0.0020 per token for long-context heavy usage
- Note: final bill depends on seq length distribution during eval spikes

2) Caching assumptions
- KV/prefix cache expected hit-rate: 18–35% (pilot median target: 25%) for templated triage flows
- We recommend instrumenting early (first 2 weeks) to gather real hit-rate; workbook has a simple estimator

3) Batching & latency tradeoffs
- Recommended batching window: 15–25ms for continuous-batching to balance throughput and P95 latency
- Typical batch size for your traffic (50–200 qps): target 8–32 tokens-per-batch; P95 SLO: 220–350ms for "small" chat, 380–600ms for "large"
- If you require P95 < 200ms, we recommend Reserved (Dedicated) capacity + smaller batch window; workbook contains cost delta estimates

4) Eval & baseline artifacts
- Included eval-prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (sample prompts, classification/regression checks). We also tokenized a pilot baseline so you can reproduce tokens/$ calculations locally.

5) MAP gating recommendations (one-pager in checklist):
- Acceptance criteria: unit econ within agreed threshold (tokens/$ within +/- 15% of workbook baseline), KV hit-rate >= 20% by week 3, and no single-request P95 spike > 2x baseline in week 1
- Rollout: canary (5% traffic) week 1, gradual ramp to 50% by week 3, full cutover after final sign-off at week 6

Attached are the workbook tabs: assumptions, live-estimator, batched-latency-sim, and a quick sensitivity table. Short answers below if you want to paste into your MAP doc.

Let me know if you want a 20-min walkthrough with procurement and engineering today or tomorrow — I can include the Live Estimator view.

Thanks,

Alicia / Priya — quick procurement follow-ups to include in your MAP: 

- Committed throughput / QPS: can you confirm expected sustained QPS during pilot peak hours? Workbook has a line-item for 50/100/200 qps scenarios but we need your best guess so we can lock reserve windows if required.
- SLA expectation: will Stellar require SLA-backed latency for P95 or just best-effort? If SLA-backed, we'll need to propose Dedicated capacity and an addendum to the MSA.

Priya — please add the short sensitivity table (sheet "sensitivity_summary") into the MAP doc so procurement can reference it. Alicia — looping Laura from Legal (cc'd) will help speed signature on the MAP addendum if Dedicated is requested.
